title: Pooled two-sample t test
biology: Evolutionary biologists compare adult beetle body length from two rearing environments.
design: Independent beetles in two rearing environments; a common population variance is a substantive model assumption.
data_characteristics: A shared population variance is assumed
question: Do mean body lengths differ between cool and warm environments?
null: The two population means are equal.
options: var.equal = TRUE requests the pooled t test
Factor order determines the difference sign
Choose the variance model deliberately; avoid a preliminary variance-test gate
assumptions: Similar approximately normal population shapes at small n
parametric: Welch tests the same mean-difference null without equal variances
Use a scientifically meaningful transformation for severe skew
nonparametric: Rank-sum changes the target to response distributions
A bootstrap interval can retain the mean-difference target

plot_args.note: Use a color for each observation
Add group means with a distinct symbol

practice: Which argument changes a Welch test into the pooled test, and what assumption have you added?
code_simulate:
set.seed(1118)
d <- data.frame(environment = rep(c("Cool", "Warm"), c(26, 30)),
                length_mm = c(rnorm(26, 10, .65), rnorm(30, 10.7, .65)))
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
beeswarm(length_mm ~ environment, data = d, pch = 21,
         bg = c("#246A73", "#B7663E"), col = "white", cex = 1.3,
         xlab = "Rearing environment", ylab = "Adult body length (mm)")
points(1:2, tapply(d$length_mm, d$environment, mean), pch = 18, cex = 2)
legend("topleft", "Group mean", pch = 18, bty = "n")
code_analysis:
d$environment <- factor(d$environment, levels = c("Cool", "Warm"))
fit <- t.test(length_mm ~ environment, data = d,
              var.equal = TRUE, conf.level = .95)
difference <- mean(d$length_mm[d$environment == "Cool"]) -
              mean(d$length_mm[d$environment == "Warm"])
generating_model: 26 independent Cool beetles are Normal(10, 0.65 SD), and 30 independent Warm beetles are Normal(10.7, 0.65 SD).
generating_truth: The true Cool minus Warm mean difference is -0.7 mm, and the two population variances are both 0.4225 mm squared.
teaching_point: Pooled and Welch t tests share the mean-difference null; their variance assumptions differ.
